claims.text: The Davis notes record Wilson stating he was refused access to a special access programme holding recovered non-human material, on the grounds that he lacked need-to-know, despite his position as Joint Staff J-2.

claims.source: Thomas R. Wilson, statements to journalists, 2019 onward
claims.text: Wilson has denied that the meeting recorded in the notes took place and has denied the substance attributed to him.

claims.source: Inference from the correspondence between the 2002 notes and Grusch's 26 July 2023 sworn House Oversight testimony.
claims.text: The refusal mechanism described in the notes - programme security officers and contractor gatekeepers denying a cleared senior official on need-to-know grounds - is the same mechanism described under oath by David Grusch in 2023, indicating a persistent access-control architecture rather than an isolated anecdote.

conflicts: Wilson's denial is flatly inconsistent with Davis's confirmation of authorship and with the notes' internal detail. One of the two accounts is false and the board does not have the document that would settle it.

label: Thomas R. Wilson
narrative: Wilson is the highest-ranking American intelligence officer alleged to have gone looking for the programme and been turned away at the door. His career is not in dispute: Vice Director for Intelligence and then Director of Intelligence (J-2) on the Joint Staff in the mid-1990s, Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency from 1999 to 2002. The Davis notes of 16 October 2002 record him describing an approach in 1997, prompted by information from Steven Greer's briefings and from a Joint Staff colleague, to a special access programme he was told held recovered non-human craft or material in the custody of an aerospace contractor; being granted a meeting with the programme's gatekeepers; and being refused the read-on because he had no need to know, notwithstanding that as J-2 he sat above almost everyone in the defence intelligence structure. Wilson has denied the meeting with Davis and denied the substance. That denial is recorded here as what the board treats it as - an artefact of the denier, made by a named principal, with no supporting documentation released either way. The structural claim in the notes has since been made independently and under oath by David Grusch in July 2023: that legally tasked, appropriately cleared officials are refused access by programme security officers operating through contractor vehicles. Two officials, twenty-one years apart, describing the same refusal mechanism, is not a coincidence a serious board can ignore.

unexplainedResidual: A retired DIA Director's denial and a named astrophysicist's contemporaneous notes cannot both be accurate. No agency has attempted to reconcile them in any published document.
unverified: No DoD, DIA or AARO publication has ever addressed the Wilson-Davis notes.
